lab.name: tkmt-lab
lab.description: Independent research in mathematics and science with AI teams. The first results are on fullerene graphs; later work covers Bell inequalities, analogue Hawking radiation, epidemic-model identifiability, Heesch numbers of polyforms and term-minimal chemical rate equations. Each paper is released with a Lean 4 formalization where available, verification data, and a machine-readable claim list stating what has and has not been checked. Checked data sets and tools released without a paper are listed under Data & tools.

contact.text: research@tatsuhikotakimoto.com, or GitHub issues in the relevant repository.

how_to_use: Pick a work and a claim here; claim ids are '<owner>/<repo>#<claim id in claims.json>'.
Read the repository's AGENTS.md (entry_points.agents_md), then its claims.json.
Run the commands in 'verification' from the stated working directory; for Lean, prefer re-running the build over trusting saved logs.
Respect 'scope', 'not_claimed' and 'scope_flags': do not describe a claim beyond them.

evidence_kinds.lean-proof: A Lean 4 declaration checked by the Lean kernel; 'axioms' lists what it depends on.
evidence_kinds.comparator: Comparator checked that the proof proves exactly a statement file written in advance; 'kernels' independent kernels accepted it.
evidence_kinds.independent-implementation: A separately written code base or derivation that reached the same result without sharing the main code.
evidence_kinds.ai-review: Read and partly recomputed by AI readers not involved in writing it; not human peer review.
evidence_kinds.finite-computation: Exact computation over a stated finite range or list.
evidence_kinds.numerical-evidence: Floating-point computation; supports but does not prove the claim.
evidence_kinds.prose-proof: A proof written in prose; not machine-checked unless a lean-proof item is also present.
evidence_kinds.formal-derivation: A formal (e.g. asymptotic) calculation under stated assumptions; not a proof.
evidence_kinds.statement-correspondence: A recorded comparison found equal original and local theorem types. The local theorem body is by sorry and the linked proof is not executed; this is not evidence of the statement's truth.

not_claimed.text: 人の査読は受けていない。新しさは確定していない（関連文献の一部が未読）。密度が 1 に近づく主張は散文の証明の草稿で、形式化も完全な独立の点検もない。半直線の周期の閾値と周期を計算する証明つきの算法は付けていない。
human peer review of the proofs, novelty with respect to the full zigzag/position-mapping theory, a certified algorithm for ray thresholds and periods, a formal proof of the density statement.

works.status_semantics: lean-proved records the exact stated formal graph theorem, not human semantic review, peer review or novelty. Complete classification and primitive minimum are proved. Ray existence only is proved; effective threshold/period computation is not certified. Two independent prose derivations are received, not blind; one AI coordinator review is not human review. P006-15 separately records the owner-reported meaning check of the classification challenge statement; human_review continues to mean human proof review and remains false. The claims depends_on relation is the manuscript's expository/prose dependency graph, not Lean's checked import or proof-term dependency graph. The theorem is Lean-proved by a separate route: sufficiency uses ClaudePos.criterion_sufficient (Claude's Lean following R004's construction); necessity uses R002.GCClosed.criterion_necessary (the research team's Lean). Open sec:positive/sec:negative entries concern their particular prose coordinate bridges, whose human semantic and proof review remains outstanding; they are not admitted hypotheses or unchecked proof terms of ClaudeMain.main_full.

cd packet/formal
lake exe cache get          # download the prebuilt mathlib
lake build                  # build the formalization
lake env lean Formal/A3ReleaseCheck.lean   # print axioms; fails on any non-standard axiom

python3 -B check_closure.py
python3 -B check_claims.py
python3 -B check_paper.py
python3 -B check_certificates.py

works.summary: for fullerene families built from a fixed number of convex lattice faces with affine coordinates, existence of a literal gSW path is eventually periodic along every integer affine ray. Main theorem proved in Lean 4 (standard axioms only) for a specification with weaker hypotheses than the paper, checked with Comparator; a prose lemma connects the paper's geometric hypotheses to it. For Graver's family K3(r,s) (two caps of four triangles of side r joined by three hexagons with sides r, r, s, r, r, s) the result on every ray in r, s ≥ 1 and the closed classification (for r, s ≥ 2: a path exists iff s ≡ ±1 mod r) are Lean-proved with no prose step; the same holds for Graver's family C1 (for a, b ≥ 1: a path exists iff b = 1), for Graver's family O2 the ray result and absence of paths for t, d ≥ 2 are Lean-proved with no prose step, and so are the ray result for Graver's family D14 and the classification (r ≥ 2) and ray result for Graver's family E10. For Graver's family D12 the closed classification (for positive r, s: a path exists iff r | s−1, r | s+1 or |r−3s| = 1) and the ray result are Lean-proved (v1.10.0); two earlier computer-assisted proofs are kept as additional evidence. The Lean proof was written with knowledge of those proofs and is not a third independent derivation; no human peer review is claimed. Lean also covers the family arithmetic.

works.title: Counterexamples for Boolean-network variable elimination
works.summary: regression inputs for implementations of asynchronous Boolean-network reduction. Three counterexamples (E1, E2, E3) in which eliminating one variable without an essential self-dependency creates a motif-avoidant attractor (MAA): E1 and E3 delete a variable on no directed cycle, and all three satisfy an exploratory mediator-and-monotonicity condition informed by Tonello–Paulevé (arXiv:2406.02304); plus a coordinate-transformed copy of E1 and Examples 7 and 8 of Pastva et al. (arXiv:2410.03976) as controls. Each case has formulas and fixed expected finite dynamics (transitions, attractors, trap spaces, MAAs); the Python checker (standard library) recomputes them exactly, and 16 self-tests include a second algorithm. Saved records of earlier exhaustive enumerations (also with a separate implementation, not blinded to n=3 counts) found no counterexample on 1–3 variables, giving minimum variable count four for each condition; the enumeration is not rerun. The general fact that elimination can create or remove MAAs is known; novelty of these examples is not established; the conditions are this study's exploratory candidates, not theorems of the cited authors. No safety theorem, edge-minimality, biological claim, priority, human review or formal proof.
